title: Teaching handwriting
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: MAN: How are you getting on with the assignment on handwriting?

WOMAN: Not too bad. You know, I hadn’t realised that children benefit in so many ways from learning to write. It’s such an important skill and yet most people think handwriting is less important than in the past because people hardly ever write by hand these days.
MAN: Yes. And all the evidence suggests children should learn to write by hand before they learn to type. Not least because it helps their memory.
WOMAN: That’s right. The physical act of writing helps children to remember letters. That seems pretty obvious when you think about it.
MAN: What’s less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration. They have to sit still and focus on one thing.
WOMAN: Yeah. That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before.
MAN: Same here. I’m not sure I understand how it improves children’s imagination though.
WOMAN: Well, there was that study which showed that primary aged children generated more ideas when they were writing by hand than using a keyboard. I would’ve guessed that would be the case.
MAN: Mmm, yeah. I’d never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either. I thought spatial awareness was more to do with knowing where you are in relation to objects or other people.

WOMAN: I thought that too. But good spatial awareness is essential for writing because you have to space words correctly. It’s not just fine motor skills that improve through writing as I’d always assumed.

MAN: Handwriting is so much harder for children with dyspraxia, who have problems coordinating movement. It’s good there are lots of things you can do in the classroom to help them. They need so much more support with letter formation – you need to play lots of games to help them distinguish letter shapes. It takes a lot of patience.
WOMAN: Yeah. I liked the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard. That seems like a really simple solution.

MAN: Yes, absolutely. I’m not sure there’s much you can do about children with dyspraxia writing very slowly. It’s more important to focus on accuracy and as they get more confident I think they eventually speed up.
WOMAN: One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper. So they write each letter in a box and that trains them to space the letters correctly.
MAN: Indeed, that’s more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line.
MAN: For some children it might be better to teach them to write on a laptop rather than by hand. Like children with dyslexia. They often really struggle with handwriting and some just give up.
WOMAN: Yeah. It’s not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong – on a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go. But I read that developing fluency isn’t any faster.
MAN: That’s right. Did you read that article on the benefits of teaching print rather than cursive handwriting, where the letters are joined up?

WOMAN: Yes. Well in the past cursive writing was certainly considered more stylish and educated. But not anymore. Teachers’ attitudes have changed because it’s been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn – especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.

MAN: I agree. I was always worried that my poor handwriting affected my exam results. And now research shows that I was right to worry. I’m sure a lot of students think it’s unfair that they’re being judged on their handwriting not just their knowledge.

WOMAN: Marks are definitely affected if examiners can’t read the script. That’s why it’s always been so important to teach children to write legibly…. Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future?

MAN: I can’t see that changing much. Touch typing still isn’t taught in most schools, which is a shame. But maybe that won’t be necessary in the future because people will also be able to write by hand on digital devices. Anyway, teachers understand the value of handwriting. It’s a basic life skill.
WOMAN: True. However, the fact is that people are writing by hand less and less and relying on digital devices. That does cause some problems.
MAN: You mean like note taking? There are lots of apps for that.

WOMAN: And for reading historical documents apparently. But my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent. I think you can put that down to lack of practice.

MAN: I expect so. Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now. I remember my grandparents had such beautiful handwriting and it was so individual. Nobody I know would be able to identify my handwriting now. It’s a shame.
WOMAN: I know. I feel the same way. I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally. It just seems less effort to do it that way. So it’s not just a problem…

Questions 21 and 22

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

questions.prompt: Which TWO benefits for children of learning to write did both students find surprising?
questions.explanation:
这部分题目中需要注意选项相关信息是否符合题干问题中的both students和surprising。原文中的hadn’t realised对应题干问题中的surprising，children原词重现，原文的动词benefit对应题干的名词benefits。

B：原文中男士提及helps their memory，对应B选项，但后续内容中女士讲到pretty obvious，与题干问题中的surprising不符，排除B。

C：之后男士讲到的less obvious对应题干问题中的surprising，相关信息为helps develop their concentration，对应C选项；女士讲到以前从未想到，never occurred to me before，其中occur to表示“（观念或想法）被想到”，男士回应Same here，两人的表述表现出surprising。因此C为正确选项之一。

D：原文中男士提及不确定自己是否理解如何improves children’s imagination，女士进一步解释有研究表明generated more ideas…，之后男士表示了认同。这些虽然对应D选项，但未体现题干问题中的both students和surprising，排除D。

E：之后男士讲到never associated spatial awareness with handwriting，对应E选项，space awareness表示“空间意识”。男士说的never associated以及后续解释说明中的I thought…，女士回应的I thought that too以及紧接着讲到But…，这些体现出原以为的情况不同，对应题干问题中的both students和surprising。因此E为正确选项之一。

A：女士讲到良好的空间意识对于书写的重要性之后，紧接着讲到不仅fine motor skills能够通过书写提升，对应A选项，fine motor skills表示“精细运动技能”。但同一句中的I’d always assumed与题干问题中的surprising不符，排除A。

因此21~22题答案为CE。

Questions 23 and 24

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

questions.prompt: For children with dyspraxia, which TWO problems with handwriting do the students think are easiest to correct?

options.text: not writing in a straight line
applying too much pressure when writing

questions.explanation:
这部分题目需要注意选项相关信息是否符合题干中的easiest to correct。在原文中children with dyspraxia和problems都原词重现，dyspraxia意为“运用障碍”。原文中coordinating对应的动词原形是coordinate，意为“使（身体部位）动作协调”。

D：原文中男士讲到的letter formation和letter shapes，对应D选项。但相关信息中，need so much more support、lots of games以及a lot of patience，都表现出并不容易，不符合题干问题中的easiest，排除D。

C：原文中女士讲到pens和press too hard，对应C选项。后续表述really simple solution对应题干问题中的easiest to correct，男士回应Yes以及absolutely。因此C为正确选项之一。

E：原文男士所述内容中，very slowly原词重现，对应E选项。但相关表述是not sure there’s much you can do，加上后续说到关注准确度更重要，不符合题干问题中的easiest to correct，排除E。

A：原文中女士讲到One quite simple thing对应题干问题中的easiest to correct。后续讲到trains them to space the letters correctly，对应A选项，男士回应Indeed。因此A为正确选项之一。

B：原文中男士所述内容中，in a straight line原词重现，对应B选项。但相关表述是more important for legibility than…，表达了相比起来清晰可读是更重要的，不符合题干问题中的easiest to correct，排除B。

因此23~24题答案为AC。

groups.instruction:
Questions 25–30

Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

Teaching handwriting

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about using laptops to teach writing to children with dyslexia?

options.text: Children often lack motivation to learn that way.
Children react more positively if they make a mistake.

questions.explanation: 本题题干中问的是What does the woman say about，需要注意正确选项与对话中女士所述内容有关。原文对话中，男士所述内容里先讲到laptop，对应题干的laptops，原文的teach them to write对应题干的teach writing，children with dyslexia原词重现。接下来提及struggle以及give up，与A选项的lack motivation有关联，但与题干问的人物woman不符，排除A。女士说到not as frustrating和more willing to have a go对应C选项的react more positively，原文的get things wrong对应选项的make a mistake。其中willing意为“乐意，愿意”，have a go表示“尝试，试图”。之后女士还提及fluency，对应B选项的fluent，但原文的isn’t any faster与选项中relatively quickly不符，排除B。因此本题答案为C。

questions.prompt: When discussing whether to teach cursive or print writing, the woman thinks that

options.text: cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children.
print writing is associated with lower academic performance.
most teachers in the UK prefer a traditional approach to handwriting.

questions.explanation: 结合题干中的woman，本题仍需注意正确选项与对话中女士所述内容有关。原文对话中，男士讲到print和cursive handwriting，对应题干中的cursive和print writing。后续内容中，女士先讲到in the past，过去的情况是，cursive writing被认为more stylish and educated，这里与B选项academic performance有关。原文以cursive writing为主语，B选项以print writing为主语，在对两者的比较中体现原文的more…和选项的lower…。但原文的past和后续讲到的not anymore，反映出与现在情况不符，排除B。女士继续讲到cursive和more difficult to learn，对应A选项中的cursive writing和disadvantages，这里的disadvantage用作动词，表示“使处于不利地位”；原文的children with learning difficulties对应选项的certain group of children。因此本题答案为A。

questions.prompt: According to the students, what impact does poor handwriting have on exam performance?

options.text: There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting.
Neat handwriting is less important now than it used to be.
Candidates write more slowly and produce shorter answers.

questions.explanation: 原文中poor handwriting和exam原词重现，对应本题题干。题干问题中问的是impact，表示“影响”，原文的affected对应题干的impact，A选项也包括affected。原文的exam results对应题干exam performance，也对应A中的grades。紧接着原文中说到research shows对应A选项的evidence。后续原文中so important对应B选项，原文的legibly对应选项的Neat，legibly是legible的副词形式，可以理解为“清晰可读地”，neat意为“整齐的，整洁的”，但这部分原文讲到的always been so important，与选项中和过去对比less important这一表述不符，排除B。因此本题答案为A。

questions.prompt: What prediction does the man make about the future of handwriting?

options.text: Touch typing will be taught before writing by hand.
Children will continue to learn to write by hand.
People will dislike handwriting on digital devices.

questions.explanation: 结合题干中的man，需要注意正确选项与对话中男士所述内容有关。原文中future原词重现，对应本题题干。女士问的具体内容是the role of handwriting未来是否将发生变化，handwriting为这部分整体讨论的主题，也同时对应本题不同选项中的writing/write by hand。男士的回应I can’t see that changing much，没有很大变化表现出B选项的continue to learn。接下来男士提及Touch typing，与A选项有关，但所述原文中isn’t taught和maybe that won’t be necessary in the future与选项不符，排除A。因此本题答案为B。

questions.prompt: The woman is concerned that relying on digital devices has made it difficult for her to
questions.explanation: 结合题干中的woman，需要注意正确选项与对话中女士所述内容有关。女士讲到relying on digital devices，对应本题题干原词，原文的That does cause some problems对应题干的concerned。后续原文中，男士提及note taking对应A选项，女士提及reading historical documents对应C选项，但这些未体现题干中的concerned或difficult，排除C。接下来在But之后，女士讲到spelling和punctuation，分别是B选项中动词spell 和punctuate对应的名词形式；原文的my awful…和inconsistent对应题干的make it difficult for her to…。因此本题答案为B。

questions.prompt: How do the students feel about their own handwriting?

options.text: concerned they are unable to write quickly
embarrassed by comments made about it
regretful that they have lost the habit

questions.explanation: 关于自己的书写，原文中男士讲到的miss和hardly ever write anything now，对应C选项的have lost the habit。后续表示It’s a shame，a shame在这里表示“令人惋惜或遗憾的事”，对应C中的regretful，意为“后悔的，失望的”。女士的回应中，I know和feel the same way表达了一致的感受。因此本题答案为C。

MAN: What’s less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration. They have to sit still and focus on one thing.

MAN: Same here. I’m not sure I understand how it improves children’s imagination though.
WOMAN: Well, there was that study which showed that primary aged children generated more ideas when they were writing by hand than using a keyboard. I would’ve guessed that would be the case.
